Assessment/Plan:
 • Melanoma cancer, stage III (s/p treatment ~23.2 years ago) - controlled; medications: none
 • Excellent follow-up and control of the malignant melanoma, stage III. The patient has been under close surveillance with no evidence of recurrence for over two decades.
 • Blood pressure and weight are stable within normal limits.
 • Review of systems reveals no new concerning symptoms.

Medical History:
 Cheryl Booth is a 52-year-old female with a long history of malignant melanoma, stage III, initially diagnosed in November 2001. She underwent treatment approximately 23.2 ago and has remained in controlled status since. Cheryl has had regular follow-up visits to monitor for any signs of recurrence.

Vital Signs:
 Recent vital signs have been stable. During the most recent visit on March 11, 2025, her blood pressure was 131/83 mmHg, and her weight was 193 pounds. Other visits have shown similar stability.

Medications:
 Currently, Cheryl is not on any medications for her melanoma. She has been managed with periodic follow-ups and monitoring without the need for ongoing pharmacological treatment.

Social History:
 Cheryl has a history of tobacco use, having smoked at a rate of 1.5 packs per day starting in March 2006. She quit smoking on February 7, 2023, and has been tobacco-free for over two years. She also consumes alcohol at a rate of approximately 10 drinks per week.

Family History:
 Cheryl’s mother had a myocardial infarction at the age of 65 years, although she did not survive to provide a definitive age at death.

Physical Examination:
 The patient appears well with no acute distress. She is ambulatory without difficulty. Vital signs are within normal limits. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal exams are unremarkable. Neurological exam is non-focal. Musculoskeletal exam reveals no tenderness or deformities. Skin examination shows no suspicious lesions.

Laboratory and Imaging:
 Recent lab results and imaging studies, including CT scans and PET scans, have been reviewed and continue to show no evidence of metastatic disease or recurrence of melanoma.

Follow-Up:
 Cheryl is scheduled for continued

regular follow-up every 6 months to monitor for signs of recurrence. She is advised to continue with routine skin examinations and to report any new symptoms immediately.

Conclusion:
 Cheryl Booth's malignant melanoma, stage III, remains in controlled status with no evidence of recurrence over the past 23.2 years. Her overall health status is stable with no new concerning symptoms or complications. Regular follow-up and monitoring will continue to be essential in maintaining her current controlled status.

Dear Colleague,

I saw Cheryl Booth in consultation on April 01, 2025. This visit was prompted by her acute sinusitis, which she has been managing with amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg. Her blood pressure was recorded at 129/89 mmHg, and her weight was 196 lbs.

Regarding her malignant melanoma, stage III, which was treated approximately 23.2 years ago, she is currently in a controlled status with no current medications required for this condition.

Ms. Booth also has a history of an inguinal hernia that was repaired on March 17, 2025. She reports that this condition is currently controlled, and no medications are needed for it.

During the visit, I noted that Ms. Booth has a history of cigarette smoking, consuming about 1.5 packs per day, which she discontinued in February 2023. Additionally, she reports consuming approximately 10 alcoholic drinks per week. She also exercises regularly, running 3-4 times per week.

Physical examination findings were otherwise unremarkable, with no abnormal findings noted.

Impression and recommendations remain as above. Thank you for this referral.
